title: Creating Fake People is a Terrible Idea - Nautilus
gist: Neuroscientist Anil Seth argues that Tavos's Griffin, a 'human interaction model' claimed to pass a video Turing Test, is a dangerous development whose social harms could exceed those of social media, from scams to exploited loneliness and eroded reality-testing.

insights.claim: Tavos, a self-described 'human computing company', announced Griffin, a 'human interaction model' it claims is the first AI product to pass a video version of the Turing Test, where people cannot tell it apart from a real person even with audio and video.
insights.speaker: Anil Seth
insights.so_what: Real-time, video-grade human simulation is being marketed as a product, marking a new capability frontier for conversational AI.
insights.quote: Supposedly, it is the first AI product to pass a video version of the Turing Test, meaning that real people cannot tell the difference between talking to Griffin and talking to a real person
insights.locator: A few days ago the “human computing company”

insights.claim: Anil Seth predicts the societal consequences of AI avatars that pass as human are likely to be disastrous, possibly worse than the harm caused by social media.
insights.speaker: Anil Seth
insights.so_what: Signals a likely backlash and regulatory pressure on human-mimicking AI, comparable to the scrutiny social platforms faced.
insights.quote: The consequences for society are likely to be disastrous—perhaps even worse than the havoc wrought by social media.

insights.claim: Human-indistinguishable AI avatars are expected to enable scams that defraud people of their savings, explode mental illness, and exploit loneliness.
insights.speaker: Anil Seth
insights.so_what: Fraud-prevention, identity verification and liveness-detection demand should rise as video-grade impersonation becomes available.
insights.quote: People will be scammed out of their savings, mental illness will explode, loneliness will be exploited.

insights.claim: Widespread use of convincing AI humans would collectively weaken people's ability to tell reality from fantasy, further straining an already stressed social fabric.
insights.speaker: Anil Seth
insights.so_what: Erosion of shared reality raises trust costs across media, commerce and politics, increasing the value of provenance and authentication.
insights.quote: Collectively we’ll become less able to tell reality from fantasy, tearing at the fabric of a society already under considerable stress.

insights.claim: Anil Seth flags that people may deliberately abuse digital avatars to indulge the darkest parts of their psychology, one of many unforeseen harms he expects.
insights.speaker: Anil Seth
insights.so_what: Unanticipated misuse categories create reputational and content-moderation liabilities for avatar companies.
insights.quote: How about people deliberately abusing their digital avatars to satisfy the darkest corners of their psychology?
